q: 1. If the iron ore contains clay as an impurity, the flux added during calcinations is .....
explain: Clay is acidic, so a basic flux such as limestone is added to combine with it and form slag.

q: 2. Pig iron obtained from the furnace which is properly provided with fuel at a very high temperature, is called .....
explain: With plenty of fuel and high temperature, carbon separates as graphite, giving grey (foundry) pig iron.

q: 3. The variety of pig iron used for the manufacture of steel by Bessemer process, is .....
explain: Bessemer pig iron, being low in sulphur and phosphorus, is used in the Bessemer process.

q: 4. The yield strength and tensile strength of low carbon steel may be improved by the addition of .....
explain: As per the answer key, vanadium. It refines grain and raises yield and tensile strength of low carbon steel.

q: 5. Stainless steel resists corrosion due to .....
explain: Chromium forms a thin, stable oxide film on the surface that protects the steel from corrosion.

q: 6. Wrought iron contains carbon upto .....
explain: Wrought iron is almost pure iron with carbon up to about 0.15%.

q: 7. Wrough iron contains carbon upto
explain: Wrought iron is a nearly pure form of iron with very low carbon content, typically up to about 0.25%.

q: 8. The process of decarbonising the pig iron completely and then adding proper percentage of carbon for manufacturing steel is called .....
explain: As per the answer key, option a. Note: this description usually matches the Bessemer or open hearth process, so the key answer looks doubtful.

q: 9. Monel metal is an alloy of .....
explain: Monel metal is mainly nickel (about 67%) and copper (about 30%).

q: 10. The proportions of copper and zinc in Muntz metal are .....
explain: Muntz metal is 60% copper and 40% zinc.

q: 11. The process of manufacturing steel by heating short lengths of wrought iron bars mixed with charcoal in the clay crucibles and collecting the molten iron into moulds, is known as .....
explain: Melting wrought iron with charcoal in clay crucibles and casting it is the crucible process.

q: 12. Galvanizing means covering iron with a thin coat of
explain: Galvanizing is the process of coating iron or steel with a protective layer of zinc to prevent rusting.

q: 13. The type of steel used for precision leveling staff, is .....
explain: Invar has almost zero thermal expansion, so it is used for precision levelling staves and measuring tapes.

q: 14. Galvanizing means covering iron with a thin coat of .....
explain: Galvanizing coats iron or steel with zinc to protect it from rust.

q: 15. The carbon content in wrought iron varies from
explain: Wrought iron has a very low carbon content, generally between 0.10% and 0.25%.

q: 16. The properties of cast iron are
options: It can be easily forged and welded
explain: Cast iron's high carbon content and brittle grain structure make it non-magnetizable, unlike wrought iron or steel.

q: 17. Cast iron contains carbon approximately .....
explain: As per the answer key, option a. Note: cast iron is usually quoted as about 2 to 4.5% carbon, so the printed range is wide.

q: 18. Wrought iron contains carbon about .....
explain: Wrought iron contains about 0.15% carbon (up to 0.15%).

q: 19. Cast iron is used for .....
explain: Cast iron is strong in compression, so it is used for columns and struts.

q: 20. The property of steel enabling it to be drawn into thin wires is called
explain: Ductility is the physical property of a material associated with the ability to be hammered thin or stretched into wire without breaking.

q: 21. The property due to which steel can withstand hammer blows is called
explain: Toughness is the ability of a material to absorb energy and deform plastically without fracturing, essential for resisting impact or hammer blows.

q: 22. Pig iron contains carbon up to
explain: Pig iron is the immediate product of smelting iron ore and has a very high carbon content, typically between 3% and 5%.

q: 23. The property of steel is influenced maximum by
explain: Carbon content is the primary factor that determines the hardness, strength, and ductility of steel.

q: 24. Purest form of iron is
explain: Wrought iron contains less than 0.15% carbon and very few impurities, making it the purest commercial form of iron.

q: 25. As compared to mild steel, cast iron has
explain: Cast iron is brittle; it is very strong in compression but fails easily under tension compared to the ductile mild steel.

q: 26. Which of the following metamorphic rocks has the most weather resisting characteristics?
explain: Quartzite's dense, interlocked quartz grains make it extremely resistant to weathering compared to marble or slate.

q: 27. Which of the following has more fire resisting characteristics?
explain: Compact sandstone withstands high temperatures better than marble, limestone, or granite, which tend to crack or decompose under fire.

q: 28. The unit weight of steel in taken as
explain: The standard density of steel used in engineering calculations is approximately 7850 kg/m3 or 7.85 ton/m3.

q: 29. Mild steel is used for
explain: Mild steel's high tensile strength and ductility make it the standard material for structural beams and reinforcement.

q: 30. The types of steel used for precision leveling staff in
explain: Invar has an extremely low coefficient of thermal expansion, ensuring that precision leveling staffs do not change length with temperature.

q: 31. Softer variety of steel may be obtained by
explain: The crucible process allows for high control over the composition, often used to produce high-quality, uniform tool steel or softer, specialized varieties.

q: 32. Bronze is as alloy of
explain: Bronze is an alloy consisting primarily of copper, usually with tin as the main additive, making it harder and more durable than pure copper.

q: 33. Invar is an alloy of
explain: Invar (FeNi36) is a nickel-iron alloy notable for its uniquely low coefficient of thermal expansion, making it essential for precision instruments.

q: 34. The main purpose of manufacture of alloys steel is to attain a certain properties like
explain: Alloying elements are added to steel to improve various characteristics, including mechanical strength, hardness, and impact resistance (toughness).

q: 35. Which of the following stresses is used for identifying the quality of structural steel?
explain: Yield stress is the key parameter used to grade and specify the quality of structural steel.

q: 36. The constituent metals of German silver are
explain: German silver is an alloy made of copper, zinc, and nickel, despite containing no actual silver.

q: 37. A prime coat is given to steel work
options: a mixture of linseed oil and red lead
explain: A prime coat of linseed oil mixed with red lead is applied to steel work as a protective anti-corrosive base layer.

q: 38. The thickness of 25 gauge sheet is
explain: A 25 gauge sheet, per standard gauge tables, corresponds to a thickness between about 1 and 1.5 mm.

q: 39. Aluminium is extensively used in aeroplane industries because
options: its tensile strength is very low
it is very tough and light metal
explain: Aluminum's high strength-to-weight ratio (tough but lightweight) makes it the primary material for aircraft construction.

q: 40. The crudest form of iron is
explain: Cast iron (or Pig iron directly from the furnace) is the crudest form, containing high carbon content and impurities.

q: 41. Depending on the chemical composition and mechanical properties, iron may be classified as
explain: Iron is classified into these three main categories based on the percentage of carbon present.
